resources.string: Capsool draws an interactive capsule around your camera cutout. It uses the accessibility service to show the capsule above other apps, to notice when the keyboard or a fullscreen app is open so it can hide, to read the name of the app in front so you can hide the capsule in chosen apps, and to open the notification shade or quick settings when you assign those actions to a gesture. Nothing is collected or sent anywhere.
Capsool needs the Accessibility permission to work. Here is exactly what it does with it.
Shows the capsule above other apps and the status bar.
Checks which windows are on screen, so the capsule hides when the keyboard or a fullscreen app (video, games) is open.
Reads the package name of the app in front, so you can hide the capsule or media card in chosen apps. Screen content and what you type are not read.
Opens the notification shade or quick settings when you assign that action to a gesture.
Capsool has no internet permission. Nothing it sees leaves your phone, and notification text is never stored.
Without the Accessibility permission Capsool cannot show the capsule. You can review the explanation again at any time.
